arrive-gangtok.title: Bagdogra / NJP → Gangtok
arrive-gangtok.alt: A traditional timber Himalayan temple complex below a ridge of snow-covered peaks
body: We meet you at Bagdogra Airport or New Jalpaiguri station and head north. The road follows the Tista almost the whole way — river on one side, terraced hillside on the other — and climbs steadily out of the plains into Sikkim.
You'll reach Gangtok in the late afternoon. After check-in the evening is yours; M.G. Marg is pedestrianised, lined with cafés, and a ten-minute walk from most hotels in town.

arrive-darjeeling.title: Bagdogra / NJP → Darjeeling
arrive-darjeeling.alt: Darjeeling town at sunrise with the snow-covered Khangchendzonga range on the horizon
body: We collect you at Bagdogra or NJP and start the climb through Kurseong, where the tea estates begin and the plains drop away behind you. It is a short drive by Himalayan standards but a steep one, and the temperature falls noticeably as you go.
Check in with the afternoon still ahead of you. Chowrasta and the Mall are walkable from most of the town, and worth an hour before dinner.

gangtok-sights.title: Gangtok, in full
gangtok-sights.alt: A traditional timber Himalayan temple complex below a ridge of snow-covered peaks
body: A full day around the town and the ridge above it: Banjhakri Falls and Bakthang Waterfall, Tashi View Point for the range on a clear morning, Gonjang Monastery, and the two hilltop shrines at Ganesh Tok and Hanuman Tok.

The afternoon covers the Flower Exhibition Centre, the Ropeway across the valley, the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology — one of the best collections of Tibetan manuscripts and thangkas anywhere — and Do Drul Chorten, ringed by its prayer wheels.
gangtok-sights.facts: FULL DAY · 10 STOPS · IN AND AROUND TOWN

tsomgo.title: Tsomgo Lake & Baba Mandir
tsomgo.alt: A turquoise high-altitude lake in North Sikkim ringed by bare slopes and snow peaks
body: An early start east towards the Nathu La road. Tsomgo sits at 3,753 m, an oval glacial lake about a kilometre long that freezes over in winter and changes colour with the season. We continue to Baba Mandir, then turn back down the same road.

This is the highest you'll go on most of our routes, and it is felt — take it slowly for the first hour up there and drink more water than you think you need. Nathu La can be added if permits are available; ask us at least two days ahead.
tsomgo.facts: 55 KM EACH WAY · 3,753 M · PERMIT REQUIRED

gangtok-to-darjeeling.title: Gangtok → Darjeeling
gangtok-to-darjeeling.alt: Darjeeling town at sunrise with the snow-covered Khangchendzonga range on the horizon
body: West out of Sikkim, back down to the Tista, across at Melli and up the other side into West Bengal. The road changes character completely on the far bank — from river gorge to tea garden within an hour.
You'll be in Darjeeling by mid-afternoon with time to settle in before an early night, because tomorrow starts at four.

gangtok-sights-to-darjeeling.title: Gangtok sights, then → Darjeeling
gangtok-sights-to-darjeeling.alt: Darjeeling town at sunrise with the snow-covered Khangchendzonga range on the horizon
body: A compressed morning in Gangtok before you leave it: Banjhakri Falls, the Flower Exhibition Centre, the Ropeway, the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Do Drul Chorten. Enough to know the town rather than pass through it.
We set off for Darjeeling after lunch, down to the Tista and across at Melli. You'll arrive with the evening free — and an early night is a good idea, because tomorrow starts at four.
gangtok-sights-to-darjeeling.facts: MORNING IN TOWN · THEN 100 KM · 4 HRS

gangtok-to-kalimpong.title: Gangtok sights, then → Kalimpong
gangtok-to-kalimpong.alt: A traditional timber Himalayan temple complex below a ridge of snow-covered peaks
body: The morning goes to Gangtok — Banjhakri Falls, the Flower Exhibition Centre, the Ropeway, the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Do Drul Chorten — and then we drive south to Kalimpong.

It is a short run, down to the river and up onto the ridge on the far side. Kalimpong sits lower and warmer than Darjeeling, and feels like a town that works for a living rather than one that receives visitors.
gangtok-to-kalimpong.facts: MORNING IN TOWN · THEN 75 KM · 2.5 HRS

kalimpong-to-darjeeling.title: Kalimpong, then → Darjeeling
kalimpong-to-darjeeling.alt: The Gorkha war memorial and obelisk at Batasia Loop, Darjeeling, with the Indian flag flying
body: A morning in Kalimpong: Deolo Hill for the view down both valleys, Durpin Monastery on the ridge, Science City, and one of the orchid nurseries the town has traded on for a century.
After lunch we climb to Darjeeling — fifty kilometres, but two hours of it, and the last stretch through tea gardens. Early night; Tiger Hill means a four o'clock start.
kalimpong-to-darjeeling.facts: MORNING IN TOWN · THEN 50 KM · 2 HRS

gangtok-to-pelling.title: Gangtok → Namchi → Ravangla → Pelling
gangtok-to-pelling.alt: The golden Buddha statue above the landscaped grounds of Buddha Park in Ravangla, South Sikkim
body: The long way west, and the better one. First Namchi, where the Chardham complex holds a 33 m Shiva above replicas of the four great pilgrimage temples. Then Ravangla, and the 40 m gilded Buddha standing over a park laid out along the ridge.
Both are worth the stop rather than the photograph. We reach Pelling in the evening — on a clear day the Khangchendzonga range is directly in front of your hotel.

pelling-sights.title: Pelling and around
pelling-sights.alt: The golden Buddha statue above the landscaped grounds of Buddha Park in Ravangla, South Sikkim
body: Start with the SkyWalk — a glass walkway out over the drop beneath the Chenrezig statue, and not for everyone. Then Rimbi Waterfalls and Khecheopalri Lake, which local belief holds is kept clear of fallen leaves by the birds.

The afternoon belongs to two things standing side by side: Pemayangtse Monastery, founded in 1705 and still one of the most important in Sikkim, and the ruins of Rabdentse, the kingdom's second capital, at the end of a short walk through forest.

gangtok-to-lachung.title: Gangtok → Lachung
gangtok-to-lachung.alt: A turquoise high-altitude lake in North Sikkim ringed by bare slopes and snow peaks
body: North Sikkim proper. Six hours for a hundred and twenty kilometres, which tells you what the road is like — Singhik for the view up the Tista gorge, then the Seven Sisters and Naga waterfalls, both of them right beside the highway.

Lachung is a village at 2,700 m where two rivers meet, and it gets cold after dark in every season. Bring a layer more than you think you need. Rooms here are simple by design; the valley is the point.

yumthang-to-gangtok.title: Yumthang Valley, then → Gangtok
yumthang-to-gangtok.alt: A turquoise high-altitude lake in North Sikkim ringed by bare slopes and snow peaks
body: An early run up to Yumthang, the Valley of Flowers, at 3,564 m — a wide flat-bottomed valley with a river down the middle and peaks on three sides. Between April and June the rhododendrons make the name obvious; the rest of the year it is bare and quiet and just as good.
There are hot springs a short walk across the river. We come back down to Lachung for lunch and continue to Gangtok, arriving in the evening.
yumthang-to-gangtok.facts: 25 KM UP · 3,564 M · THEN 120 KM BACK

darjeeling-sights.title: Tiger Hill, then the town
darjeeling-sights.alt: The Khangchendzonga range catching first light above Darjeeling
body: We leave at four. Tiger Hill is 2,590 m and about forty minutes out, and on a clear morning Khangchendzonga catches the light a good while before the valley does — first pink, then white. On the clearest days you can pick out Everest to the west.

Coming back we stop at Ghoom Monastery and at Batasia Loop, where the toy train turns a full circle around the Gorkha war memorial. After breakfast: the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, the Padmaja Naidu zoological park next door, the Ropeway, Tenzing Rock, a working tea garden, and the Japanese Peace Pagoda to close the day.

mirik.title: Mirik & the Nepal border
mirik.alt: Darjeeling town at sunrise with the snow-covered Khangchendzonga range on the horizon
body: South through pine forest and tea estate to Mirik, where the lake sits in a bowl of cypress with a footbridge across the middle and a path all the way round it.
We carry on to the Simana and Gopaldhara viewpoints, then to Pashupati Market, which is over the line in Nepal. Carry cash and a photo ID; crossing is routine but the shops are not set up for cards.

depart-gangtok.title: Gangtok → Bagdogra / NJP
depart-gangtok.alt: A traditional timber Himalayan temple complex below a ridge of snow-covered peaks
body: Check out after breakfast and back down the Tista to Bagdogra or NJP. Tell us your flight or train time the evening before and we will set the departure with real margin — the road is good but it is a mountain road, and it does not like being hurried.

depart-darjeeling.title: Darjeeling → Bagdogra / NJP
depart-darjeeling.alt: Darjeeling town at sunrise with the snow-covered Khangchendzonga range on the horizon
body: Down through Kurseong and the tea gardens to Bagdogra or NJP. Give us your flight or train time the night before and we will set the departure with real margin — the descent is quicker than the climb, but not by as much as people expect.

depart-pelling.title: Pelling → Bagdogra / NJP
depart-pelling.alt: The golden Buddha statue above the landscaped grounds of Buddha Park in Ravangla, South Sikkim
body: Out of West Sikkim and down to the plains — a longer run than the Gangtok departure, so we usually start earlier. Confirm your flight or train time with us the evening before and we will work back from it.
